\section{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Contraction}

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Contraction: Introduction}
Two-valued vectors reduce weighted finite-noise contraction to a two-point estimate. Normalization and the extremal-vector result give the sharp inequality for every finite probability vector.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Sharp --- Finite Noise Contraction: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted sum of a two-valued function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set with real weights satisfying $\sum_iw_i=1$. Suppose
$f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ takes only the values $a$ and $b$, for some $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, and
let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$. With $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$, one has
\[
\sum_iw_i\varphi(f_i)=\gamma\varphi(a)+(1-\gamma)\varphi(b).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mass dichotomy for two-valued functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_mass_dichotomy}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i>0$ and $\sum_iw_i=1$. Suppose $\lambda>0$,
$w_i\ge\lambda$ for every $i$, and $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ takes only the values $a$ and $b$,
where $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$. Then either $f$ is identically
$a$, $f$ is identically $b$, or $\lambda\le\gamma\le1-\lambda$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp finite noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_sharp_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.exists_nonnegative_noise_maximizer, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_contraction_of_unit_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_two_values, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_mass_dichotomy, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.weighted_two_point_le_of_atom_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}

Let $I$ be a finite set with real weights satisfying $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $q>2$ and
$0<\lambda<1/2$, with $w_i\ge\lambda$ for every $i$. Put $p=q/(q-1)$ and let $\rho$ be
the sharp discrete radius at $(q,\lambda)$. Then every $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies
\[
\rho^2\sum_iw_i f_i^2+(1-\rho^2)\left(\sum_iw_i
f_i\right)^2\le\left(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p\right)^{2/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}
